column3: I say then, God did not reject his people, did he? Certainly not! For I too am an Israelite, from the offspring of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
God did not reject his people whom he foreknew. Or do you not know what Scripture says in the passage about Elijah, how he appeals to God against Israel?
“Lord, they killed your prophets, they tore down your altars, and I alone was left, and they are seeking my life.”
But what does the divine response say to him? “I have left for myself seven thousand men who did not bow the knee to Baal.”
So then, also in the present time there has come to be a remnant according to election of grace.
But if by grace, it is no longer from works; otherwise grace is no longer grace.
What then? What Israel seeks, this it did not obtain, but the chosen obtained it; and the rest were hardened,
just as it is written, “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes so as not to see and ears so as not to hear, until this very day.”
And David says, “Let their table become a snare and a trap and a stumbling block and a repayment to them;
let their eyes be darkened so as not to see, and bend their back continually.”
I say then, they did not stumble so as to fall, did they? Certainly not! But by their trespass salvation came to the Gentiles, to make them jealous.
Now if their trespass is riches for the world and their failure riches for the Gentiles, how much more their fullness?
Now I speak to you Gentiles. Insofar as I am an apostle of Gentiles, I glorify my ministry,
if somehow I might make my flesh jealous and save some from among them.
For if their rejection is reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance be if not life from the dead?
And if the firstfruits are holy, so also the lump; and if the root is holy, so also the branches.
But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them and became a fellow sharer of the root of the richness of the olive tree,
do not boast against the branches. But if you boast, remember that you do not support the root, but the root supports you.
You will say then, “Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.”
True. They were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not think high things, but fear.
For if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.
See then the kindness and severity of God: severity toward those who fell, but God’s kindness toward you, if you remain in the kindness; otherwise you also will be cut off.
And they also, if they do not remain in unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.

For if you were cut from what is by nature a wild olive tree and, contrary to nature, were grafted into a cultivated olive tree, how much more will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?

For I do not want you to be unaware of this mystery, brothers and sisters, so that you may not be wise in yourselves: a partial hardening has happened to Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in,
and in this way all Israel will be saved, just as it is written, “The Deliverer will come from Zion; he will turn ungodliness away from Jacob.
And this is my covenant with them, when I take away their sins.”
According to the good news they are enemies for your sake, but according to election they are loved for the sake of the fathers,
for the gracious gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
For just as you once disobeyed God but now received mercy because of their disobedience,
so these also now disobeyed because of the mercy shown to you, so that they themselves also may now receive mercy.
For God shut up all in disobedience so that he might show mercy to all.
Oh, the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable his judgments and untraceable his ways!
“For who knew the mind of the Lord, or who became his counselor?
Or who first gave to him, and it will be repaid to him?”
Because from him and through him and to him are all things. To him be the glory forever. Amen.
